scope: Read-only manipulation-example screen, live nearest PR status, and common benchmark overlap. Source snapshots only; no builds, claims or submissions.
conclusion: Borrow contact models, constraints, diagnostic scenes and validation patterns. No direct example copy is recommended for submission. Two toy directions are conditional research candidates; three entries are reusable mechanisms only. None is ready.

ranked.borrow: Two-way coupling between rigid fingers/objects and deformable material; measured settling and repeated outcome checks. Potential to investigate currently impossible material interactions rather than substituting rigid proxies.
critical_findings: cloth_block cloth is pinned along two edges; it is not a free cloth-sling carry demonstration.
shirt_fold_stack changes finger friction from script phase and commanded pinch state (lines507–509); material switching must not be copied as a physical-world claim.
Its own header says cloth grasps are nondeterministic; a gallery video is not two validated task demos.
ranked.novelty: Do not submit T-shirt folding: directly overlaps BEHAVIOR folding and published YAM folding. Cloth sling cake2298 was final rejected as insufficiently relatable/simple.
ranked.gate: Show a real material law, constant physical material parameters and physical contact grasp/release at commercial dimensions before making any new task claim.

ranked.direction: Load-sensitive friction and realistic pinch torsion
ranked.borrow: Small isolated force-displacement diagnostics for loaded hinges, contact torsion and actuator force limits; suitable for testing whether relieving load genuinely changes release difficulty.
ranked.novelty: Adding this physics to an ordinary held-while-turning task is not enough for novelty. Do not rename objects to invent tasks.
ranked.gate: Calibrate to hardware curves and make same failure/success routes work with native physics; compare present PhysX model without assuming Steel parameters transfer.

ranked.direction: Launch an ordinary free-spinning top through contact and release it upright
ranked.kind: conditional ordinary-task direction; feasibility and importance unproven
ranked.borrow: Free-body gyroscopic persistence, tip/floor friction and release observation.
critical_findings: Exported scene explicitly uses ur10+rotary_chuck and extra driven coordinates. It is not a two-finger YAM spin demo.
Must identify a real, obtainable finger top or pull-cord top and preserve its actual stem/cord mechanism; no powered-chuck substitution for claimed hand launch.
ranked.novelty: Fresh searches found no exact spinning-top PR. Nearby2722 Twister spinner is pending: fixed-axis flick versus freely balanced gyro is a genuine physical distinction, but it is only a candidate distinction.
ranked.acceptance_risk: Board2862 card-house puzzle final rejected for lacking real-world impact; recreational precedent is mixed. Do not present top as cleared simply because it looks impressive.
ranked.gate: Real dimensions, YAM attainable angular speed, no post-release motor force, observable numeric persistence and safe ordinary play relevance. Stop if only motorized launch works or importance remains a generic physics puzzle.

ranked.direction: Closed-loop linkage manipulation, illustrated by Hoberman sphere
ranked.kind: reusable constraint mechanism; toy task is low-priority research
ranked.borrow: Graph construction of real closed loops, loop-closure error checks, and comparison to exact kinematics.
critical_findings: Hoberman has120 bars,240 hinges,91 independent loops.
Source explicitly sets zero gravity/no contact and an internal hub drive.
Source says ground variant omitted because the hub drive cannot open it against gravity/floor friction.
ranked.novelty: Fresh Hoberman/expanding-sphere searches found no exact task. Expanding a commercial toy with external hand contacts could differ from existing hinge folding, but the present example proves no such capability.
ranked.gate: Commercial dimensions and connector topology; normal gravity and floor contacts; all internal hub drives removed; both external grasps reach and remain contact-based; real importance beyond a linkage demo. Kill if geometry/forces require toy rescaling or hidden drives.

ranked.direction: Mesh/SDF contact for physically engaged threads and thin curved fixtures
ranked.borrow: SDF collision cooking/cache, mesh-to-contact checks and contact-driven engagement instead of writing poses or prescribing insertion.
critical_findings: Nut/bolt source loads assets/factory/mesh/factory_nut_bolt from IsaacGym Factory; ordinary nut-on-bolt is already a standard benchmark family.
Solver/contact improvements do not make the same assembly operation a novel task.
ranked.gate: Choose an independently important distinct real operation first. Verify mesh dimensions, license and contact convergence; keep all valid alternative execution routes.

direct_copy_exclusions.reason: Already claimed wooden coupled train pushed round bend; changing engine/wagon assets is superficial.
Stacking puzzle without demonstrated impact; more cards is not a substantive answer.
Review explicitly identifies dexhand Sweep Dustpan overlap. More debris or nuts instead of crumbs is not novelty.
Do not rename pinned-cloth demo as cake sling carry; actual sling candidate already rejected.
Common drawer/pick-place, kitchen appliance and laundry-folding operations already represented in LIBERO/RoboCasa/BEHAVIOR; extra props or changed colors do not distinguish skills.

integration_and_license: Steel examples run in Newton, currently pinned to skild-ai/newton. They are not drop-in IsaacLab task files. Root/example Apache-2.0 does not supersede optional mesh/media licenses; preserve component notices and inspect examples/THIRD_PARTY.md. Existing YAM/Inspect compatibility must be demonstrated before adopting another solver.
recommended_action: Use mechanism examples to answer specific physical blockers in an acceptance-worthy task. Do not pause validated existing tasks for wholesale solver migration; no immediate new submission is supported by this screen.
